newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise, spread to bund narrows.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise, spread to bund narrows.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Thursday, with what dealers said was healthy foreign and local interest and the 10-year spread to the German bund narrowed.

At 1210 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.64, yielding 6.08 percent, from Tuesday's 112.35. The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark on September 1, rose to 105.22, yielding 6.29 percent, from 104.95.

The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund narrowed two basis points to 42 and the 2007 gap to the bund shrank by the same amount to 62 bp. "We expect the gap to narrow and test 60 bp by the weekend," a dealer said.
Turnover in the benchmark was 2.5 billion crowns and the 2007 saw volume of three billion.
The two-10 year curve flattened slightly to 245 bp.
The crown weakened to 3.8091 to the mark from 3.8081.
The benchmark bond's September future rose 0.33 point to 111.88 with 33 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.35 point to 91.05.

Realkredit Danmark earlier auctioned one billion crowns worth of its six percent 1998 mortgage-backed bond at 101.052 and 269 million in its six percent 1999 at 102.85. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
